short: A supreme allied commander who spent eight years restraining American force.
full:
Eisenhower ended the Korean War with an armistice in July 1953, six months after taking office, and kept the United States out of Indochina in 1954 despite pressure to relieve the French at Dien Bien Phu. He relied on nuclear deterrence and covert action, the CIA overturning governments in Iran in 1953 and Guatemala in 1954, to hold down conventional defence spending.

At home he signed the Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956, which built some 41,000 miles of interstate, and sent the 101st Airborne into Little Rock in 1957 to enforce school desegregation after the governor of Arkansas defied a federal court. The Soviet launch of Sputnik that year prompted the creation of NASA and a rebuilt science curriculum. His farewell address in January 1961 warned against the influence of what he named the military-industrial complex.
